questions.q: Let $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$. If $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$ and $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The given integral is $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$.

Factorizing the denominator, we get $x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x + 5)(x - 3)$.

Using partial fractions, we can write:

$\dfrac{16x + 24}{(x + 5)(x - 3)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 5} + \dfrac{B}{x - 3}$

$16x + 24 = A(x - 3) + B(x + 5)$

Substituting $x = 3$, we get $72 = 8B \Rightarrow B = 9$.

Substituting $x = -5$, we get $-56 = -8A \Rightarrow A = 7$.

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{7}{x + 5} + \dfrac{9}{x - 3}\right) dx$

$f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3| + C$

Given $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we substitute $x = 4$:

$f(4) = 7 \log_e(9) + 9 \log_e(1) + C = 14 \log_e(3) + C$

Since $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we get $C = 0$.

Thus, $f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3|$.

Now, substituting $x = 7$:

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(12) + 9 \log_e(4)$

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(2^2 \cdot 3) + 9 \log_e(2^2)$

$f(7) = 7(2 \log_e(2) + \log_e(3)) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 14 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 32 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3)$

$f(7) = \log_e(2^{32} \cdot 3^7)$

Comparing this with $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, we get $\alpha = 32$ and $\beta = 7$.

Therefore, $\alpha + \beta = 32 + 7 = 39$.

Answer: $39$

Let $f(t)=\int\left(\frac{1-\sin \left(\log _{e} t\right)}{1-\cos \left(\log _{e} t\right)}\right) d t, t>1$.
If $f\left(e^{\pi / 2}\right)=-e^{\pi / 2}$ and $f\left(e^{\pi / 4}\right)=\alpha e^{\pi / 4}$, then $\alpha$ equals
questions.solution:
Substituting $u = \log t$ with $dt = e^u du$:
$f(t) = \int \frac{1 - \sin u}{1 - \cos u} e^u du$
Express as: $\frac{1 - \sin u}{1 - \cos u} = \frac{1}{2}\csc^2(u/2) - \cot(u/2)$
Using integration by parts and standard techniques:
$f(t) = e^{\log t}\cot(\frac{\log t}{2}) + C = t\cot(\frac{\log t}{2}) + C$
From $f(e^{\pi/2}) = -e^{\pi/2}$:
$e^{\pi/2}\cot(\pi/4) + C = -e^{\pi/2}$ → $e^{\pi/2} + C = -e^{\pi/2}$ → $C = -2e^{\pi/2}$
For $f(e^{\pi/4})$: $f(e^{\pi/4}) = e^{\pi/4}\cot(\pi/8) - 2e^{\pi/2}$
With $\cot(\pi/8) = 1 + \sqrt{2}$: $\alpha = -1 - \sqrt{2}$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{I}(x)=\int \frac{3 d x}{(4 x+6)\left(\sqrt{4 x^{2}+8 x+3}\right)}$ and $\mathrm{I}(0)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+20$. If $\mathrm{I}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{a \sqrt{2}}{b}+\mathrm{c}$, where $a, b, \mathrm{c} \in \mathrm{N}, \operatorname{gcd}(a, b)=1$, then $a+b+c$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$4x^2+8x+3 = (2x+1)(2x+3)$ and $4x+6 = 2(2x+3)$.
$I(x) = \frac{3}{4}\int \frac{du}{u^{3/2}\sqrt{u-2}}$ where $u = 2x+3$.
Substituting $u = 2\sec^2\phi$: $I(x) = \frac{3}{4}\sin\phi + C = \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2x+1}{2x+3}} + C$.
$I(0) = \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} + C = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} + C = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} + 20 \Rightarrow C = 20$.
$I\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{4}} + 20 = \frac{3}{4\sqrt{2}} + 20 = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{8} + 20$.
$a = 3, b = 8, c = 20$, $\gcd(3,8) = 1$. $a+b+c = 31$.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\int \frac{\left(2-x^{2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{e}^{x}}{(\sqrt{1+x})(1-x)^{3 / 2}} \mathrm{~d} x$. If $f(0)=0$, then $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Write $2 - x^2 = (1-x)(1+x) + 1$, so the integrand splits as $e^x\left(\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x}(1-x)^{3/2}}\right)$.
Let $g(x) = \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}$. Then $g'(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x}(1-x)^{3/2}}$.
Using $\int e^x(g + g')dx = e^x g + C$: $f(x) = e^x\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}} + C$.
$f(0) = 1 + C = 0 \Rightarrow C = -1$.
$f(1/2) = e^{1/2}\sqrt{\frac{3/2}{1/2}} - 1 = \sqrt{e}\cdot\sqrt{3} - 1 = \sqrt{3e} - 1$.

questions.q: If $\begin{aligned} \int\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^3}\right) & \left(\sqrt[23]{3 x^{-24}+x^{-26}}\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{\alpha}{3(\alpha+1)}\left(3 x^\beta+x^\gamma\right)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha}}+C, x \gt 0,\end{aligned} (\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in Z)$, where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to ________ .
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^4}\right)\left(\frac{3}{\mathrm{x}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)^{\frac{1}{23}} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \text{ using } \mathrm{t}=\frac{3}{\mathrm{x}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{dt}=-3\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^4}\right) \mathrm{dx} \\ & \int \frac{\mathrm{t}^{1 / 23} \mathrm{dt}}{-3}=\frac{\mathrm{t}^{24 / 23}}{\left(\frac{24}{23}\right)(-3)}+C \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=23 \beta=-1 \gamma=-3 \\ & \alpha+\beta+\gamma=19\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{10}}{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)^9} d x= \frac{1}{m}\left(\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^n\left(n \sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)\right)+C \text{ where } C$is the constant of integration and $m, n \in N$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}  is equal to$
questions.solution:
rationalise
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \int \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{10}}{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)^9} \times \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^9}{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^9} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \int \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{19}}{1} d x
\end{aligned}$
Put $\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}+\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t}$
$\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}}+1\right) \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dt}$
$\mathrm{dx}=\frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t}} \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}$
Now as $\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}+\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ so } \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}-\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}} \\ & \therefore \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Thus $I=\int \mathrm{t}^{19} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}\right)$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int\left(\mathrm{t}^{19}+\mathrm{t}^{17}\right) \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{t}^{20}}{20}+\frac{\mathrm{t}^{18}}{18}\right)+\mathrm{C} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{t}^{19}}{360}\left[9 \mathrm{t}+\frac{10}{\mathrm{t}}\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{t}^{19}}{360}\left[9\left(\mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}\right)+\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}+\mathrm{x}\right)^{19}}{360}\left[9\left(2 \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}\right)+\left(\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}-\mathrm{x}\right)\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}+\mathrm{x}\right)^{19}}{360}\left[19 \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}-\mathrm{x}\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{~m}=360, \mathrm{n}=19 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{n}=379
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 2 \mathrm{x}^2+5 \mathrm{x}+9=\mathrm{A}\left(\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1\right)+\mathrm{B}(2 \mathrm{x}+1)+\mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{A}=2 \quad \mathrm{~B}=\frac{3}{2} \quad \mathrm{C}=\frac{11}{2} \\ & 2 \int \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1} \mathrm{dx}+\frac{3}{2} \int \frac{2 \mathrm{x}+1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}} \mathrm{dx}+\frac{11}{2} \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}} \\ & 2 \int \sqrt{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} \mathrm{dx}+3 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}+\frac{11}{2} \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}} \\ & 2\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}\right)\right)+3 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1} \\ & +\frac{11}{2} \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}+1}\right)+\mathrm{C} \\ & \alpha=\frac{7}{2} \quad\beta=\frac{25}{4} \\& \alpha+2 \beta=16 \\ &  \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\int x^3 \sin x \mathrm{~d} x=g(x)+C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. If $8\left(g\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+g^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=\alpha \pi^3+\beta \pi^2+\gamma, \alpha, \beta, \gamma \in Z$, then $\alpha+\beta-\gamma$ equals :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \int x^3 \sin x d x=-x^3 \cos x+\int 3 x^2 \cos x d x \\
& =-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x-\int 6 x \sin x d x \\
& =-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x+6 x \cos x-6 \sin x+c
\end{aligned}$

So $g(x)=-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x+6 x \cos x-6 \sin x \begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{g}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{3 \pi^2}{4}-6 \\
& \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-3 \mathrm{x}^2 \cos \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{x}^3 \sin \mathrm{x}+6 \cos \mathrm{x}-6 \cos \mathrm{x} \\
& \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi^3}{8} \\
& 8\left(\mathrm{~g}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+\mathrm{g}^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=\pi^3+6 \pi^2-48
\end{aligned}$

So $\alpha+\beta-\gamma=55$

questions.q: Let $\int \frac{2-\tan x}{3+\tan x} \mathrm{~d} x=\frac{1}{2}\left(\alpha x+\log _{\mathrm{e}}|\beta \sin x+\gamma \cos x|\right)+C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. Then $\alpha+\frac{\gamma}{\beta}$ is equal to :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{2-\tan x}{3+\tan x} d x=\int \frac{2 \cos x-\sin x}{3 \cos x+\sin x} d x \\ & 2 \cos x-\sin x=A(3 \cos x+\sin x)+B(\cos x-3 \sin x) \\ & 3 A+B=2 \\ & A-3 B=-1\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2}, B=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \therefore \int \frac{2 \cos x-\sin x}{3 \cos x+\sin x} d x \\ & =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \ln |3 \cos x+\sin x|+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2}(x+\ln |3 \cos x+\sin x|)+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2}(\alpha x+\ln |\beta \sin x+\gamma \cos x|)+C \\ & \alpha=1, \beta=1, \gamma=3 \\ & \therefore \alpha+\frac{\gamma}{\beta}=1+\frac{3}{1}=4\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{(x-1)^4(x+3)^6}} d x=A\left(\frac{\alpha x-1}{\beta x+3}\right)^B+C \\ & I=\int \frac{1}{(x-1)^{4 / 5}(x+3)^{6 / 5}} d x \\ & I=\int \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)^{4 / 5}(x+3)^2} d x \\ & \left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)=t \Rightarrow \frac{4}{(x+3)^2} d x=d t \quad t^{-4 / 5+1} \\ & I=\frac{1}{4} \int \frac{1}{t^{4 / 5}} d t=\frac{1}{4} \frac{t^{1 / 5}}{1 / 5}+c \\ & I=\frac{5}{4}\left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)^{1 / 5}+C \\ & A=\frac{5}{4} \quad \alpha=\beta=1 \quad B=\frac{1}{5} \\ & \alpha+\beta+20 A B=2+20 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{1}{5}=7\end{aligned}$

If $\int \operatorname{cosec}^5 x d x=\alpha \cot x \operatorname{cosec} x\left(\operatorname{cossc}^2 x+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\beta \log _\epsilon\left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+C$
where $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $8(\alpha+\beta)$ equals _______
questions.solution:
$\int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x \cdot \operatorname{cosec}^2 x d x=I$
By applying integration by parts $\begin{aligned} & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x+\int \cot x\left(-3 \operatorname{cosec}^2 x \cot x \operatorname{cosec} x\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) d x \\ & I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-3 I+3 \int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x \end{aligned}$ let $\begin{aligned} & I_1=\int \operatorname{cosec}^3 x d x=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int \cot ^2 x \operatorname{cosec} x d x \\ & I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x-\int\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-1\right) \operatorname{cosec} x d x \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & 2 I_1=-\operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & I_1=-\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right| \\ & 4 I=-\cot x \operatorname{cosec}^3 x-\frac{3}{2} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x+\frac{3}{2} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+4 c \\ & I=-\frac{1}{4} \operatorname{cosec} x \cot x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left|\tan \frac{x}{2}\right|+c \\ & \therefore \alpha=\frac{-1}{4}, \beta=\frac{3}{8} \rightarrow 8(\alpha+\beta)=1\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{3}xsin ( x - \theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{3}x ( sinxcos\theta - cosxsin\theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sqrt{\sin^{3}x\cos^{4}x ( tanxcos\theta - sin\theta )}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x}{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x\cos^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{\sin^{2}xcos\dfrac{3}{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{1}{\sin^{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{{cosec}^{2}x}{\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

So, $I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} . . . . \left\{let\right\}$

For ${I}_{1}$, let $tanxcos\theta - sin\theta = {t}^{2}$

$⇒ cos\theta \times {sec}^{2}xdx = 2tdt$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta}$

For ${I}_{2}$, let $cos\theta - cotxsin\theta = {z}^{2}$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}x \times sin\thetadx = 2zdz$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta}$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta \times t} + ∫ \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta \times z}$

$⇒ I = 2\left[\left(sec\theta\right) ∫ \left(1\right)dt + cosec\theta ∫ \left(1\right)dz\right]$

$⇒ I = 2sec\theta\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta} + 2 cosec \theta\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 4sec\thetacosec\theta$

$⇒ A \times B = \dfrac{2}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{sin\thetacos\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 8 cosec 2\theta$

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{\left({x}^{8} - {x}^{2}\right)dx}{\left({x}^{12} + 3{x}^{6} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{8} - {x}^{2}}{\left({x}^{12} + 3{x}^{6} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}dx$

Putting, $\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right) = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 + {\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{2}} \cdot \left(3{x}^{2} - \dfrac{3}{{x}^{4}}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 + \left({x}^{6} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{6}} + 2\right)} \cdot \left(3{x}^{2} - \dfrac{3}{{x}^{4}}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{6}}{{x}^{12} + 3{x}^{6} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{3{x}^{6} - 3}{{x}^{4}}dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left({x}^{8} - {x}^{2}\right)}{{x}^{12} + 3{x}^{6} + 1}dx = \dfrac{dt}{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{1}{t}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3}log | t | + C$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3}log\left|\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)\right| + C$

$⇒ I = log\left|\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)\right|\dfrac{1}{3} + C$

Hence optin $\left(A\right)$ is correct

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(3 + 4{x}^{2}\right)\sqrt{4 - 3{x}^{2}}}, \left|x\right| < \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$. If $f\left(0\right) = 0$ and $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{\alpha\beta}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}\right), \alpha, \beta > 0$, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(3 + 4{x}^{2}\right)\sqrt{4 - 3{x}^{2}}}$

Put $x = \dfrac{1}{t}, dx = - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}dt$

So, $f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- dt}{{t}^{2}\left(3 + \dfrac{4}{{t}^{2}}\right)\sqrt{4 - \dfrac{3}{{t}^{2}}}}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- tdt}{\left(3{t}^{2} + 4\right)\sqrt{4{t}^{2} - 3}}$

Now let, $4{t}^{2} - 3 = {\lambda}^{2} ⇒ 8tdt = 2\lambdad\lambda$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - ∫ \dfrac{\lambdad\lambda}{4 \cdot \left(3\left(\dfrac{{\lambda}^{2} + 3}{4}\right) + 4\right) \cdot \lambda}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - ∫ \dfrac{d\lambda}{3{\lambda}^{2} + 9 + 16}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - ∫ \dfrac{d\lambda}{3{\lambda}^{2} + 25}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{d\lambda}{{\lambda}^{2} + \dfrac{25}{3}}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\lambda}{5}\right) + c$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{15}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{\left(4 - 3{x}^{2}\right)}}{5x}\right) + c$

Now using, $f\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{30}$

Hence, $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{15}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\right) + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{15} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{15}\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{15}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\right)\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{15}{cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{15}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

Now comparing with given value of $f\left(1\right)$ we get, $\alpha = 5 \text{ and } \beta = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = 28$

questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\infty}\left(\dfrac{6}{{e}^{3x} + 6{e}^{2x} + 11{e}^{x} + 6}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{6}{\left({e}^{x} + 1\right)\left({e}^{x} + 2\right)\left({e}^{x} + 3\right)}dx$

Using partial fraction, we can write

$⇒ I = 6{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\left[\dfrac{1}{2\left({e}^{x} + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{\left({e}^{x} + 2\right)} + \dfrac{1}{2\left({e}^{x} + 3\right)}\right]dx$

$⇒ I = 6{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\left[\dfrac{1}{2\left({e}^{- x} + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{\left(1 + 2{e}^{- x}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{2\left(1 + 3{e}^{- x}\right)}\right]{e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ I = 6{\left[- \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}\left({e}^{- x} + 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}\left(2{e}^{- x} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{6}{\log}_{e}\left(3{e}^{- x} + 1\right)\right]}_{0}^{\infty}$

$⇒ I = 6\left[0 - \left\{- \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}2 + \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}3 - \dfrac{1}{6}{\log}_{e}4\right\}\right]$

$⇒ I = 3{\log}_{e}2 - 3{\log}_{e}3 + {\log}_{e}4$

$⇒ I = 5{\log}_{e}2 - 3{\log}_{e}3$

$⇒ I = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{32}{27}\right)$

questions.q: Let $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$ and $I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7{\log}_{e}7$. If $I\left(1\right) = \alpha + 7{\log}_{e}\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right),$ then ${\alpha}^{4}$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$

Now let, $\dfrac{x + 7}{x} = {t}^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{7}{{x}^{2}}dx = 2tdt$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{- 14t}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left({t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}} - 2\right)}$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 14}{2} ∫ \left[\dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} - 4} + \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2}}\right]dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 7\left(\dfrac{1}{4}ln\left|\dfrac{t + \dfrac{1}{t} - 2}{t + \dfrac{1}{t} + 2}\right| - \dfrac{1}{t - \dfrac{1}{t}}\right) + c$

Now when $x = 9, t = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7 \times ln7 = \dfrac{- 7}{4}ln{\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \dfrac{12}{7} + c$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

Now when $x = 1, t = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = + \dfrac{7}{4}ln{\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2} - 1}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{7} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{7}{2}ln\left(\dfrac{{\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{7}\right) + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = 7ln\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right) - \dfrac{7}{2}ln7 + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ \alpha = 2\sqrt{2} ⇒ {\alpha}^{4} = 64$

questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$

Now let $I = ∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx$

Now let ${\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} = t$

$⇒ 2x\left(lnx - 1\right) = lnt$

$⇒ lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{2t}dt$

So, $I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} - {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right) + C$

Hence, $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta = 2 + 4 + 6 - 8 = 4$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.q: If $I\left(x\right) = ∫ {e}^{\sin^{2}x}\left(cosxsin2x - sinx\right)dx$ and $I\left(0\right) = 1$, then $I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ {e}^{\sin^{2}x}\left(cosxsin2x - sinx\right)dx$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ {e}^{\sin^{2}x}\left(cosx - \dfrac{1}{2cosx}\right)sin2xdx$

Now let, $\sin^{2}x = t ⇒ sin2xdx = dt$

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ {e}^{t}\left(\sqrt{1 - t} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - t}}\right)dt$

Now comparing with,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ {e}^{t}\left(f\left(t\right) + {f}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt = {e}^{t}f\left(t\right) + c$

Here, $f\left(t\right) = \sqrt{1 - t} \text{ and } {f}^{'}\left(t\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - t}}$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = {e}^{t}\sqrt{1 - t} + c = {e}^{\sin^{2}x} \cdot cosx + c$

Now using, $I\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 0$

Hence, the value of $I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}e\dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: Let $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx, x > 0 .$ If $\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$ then $I\left(1\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Now let $1 + x{e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\left(x + 1\right)dx = dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{2}}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- \left(t + 1\right)}{{t}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ - \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - lnt + \dfrac{1}{t} + ln\left(t - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{x{e}^{x}}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C$

Also given,$\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[ln\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C\right]$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \left[ln\left(1 - 0\right) + 0 + C\right]$

$⇒ C = 0$

Now finding,

$I\left(1\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{e}{e + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} - ln ( e + 1 )$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{e + 2}{e + 1} - ln\left(e + 1\right)$

questions.solution:
Given that $I\left(x\right) = ∫ {x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x{sec}^{2}x + tanx}{( xtanx + 1{)}^{2}}\right)dx$

Apply Integration by parts.

$∫ f\left(x\right)g\left(x\right)dx = f\left(x\right) ∫ g\left(x\right)dx - ∫ \left(f ' \left(x\right) ∫ g\left(x\right)dx\right)dx$

$= {x}^{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{x{sec}^{2}x + tanx}{( xtanx + 1{)}^{2}}\right)dx - ∫ \left(\dfrac{d {x}^{2}}{d x} ∫ \left(\dfrac{x{sec}^{2}x + tanx}{( xtanx + 1{)}^{2}}\right)dx\right)dx$

Let $xtanx + 1 = p$

$⇒ \left(x{sec}^{2}x + tanx\right)dp = dx$

$= {x}^{2} ∫ \dfrac{dp}{{p}^{2}} - ∫ \left(2x ∫ \dfrac{dp}{{p}^{2}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{- {x}^{2}}{( xtanx + 1 )} + ∫ \dfrac{2x}{xtanx + 1}dx$

Let ${I}_{1} = 2 ∫ \dfrac{x}{xtanx + 1}dx$

$= 2 ∫ \dfrac{xcosx}{xsinx + cosx}dx$

Let $xsinx + cosx = t$

$⇒ ( xcosx + sinx - sinx ) dx = dt$

$⇒ ( xcosx ) dx = dt$

$= 2 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{t} = 2logt + c$

$= 2log | xsinx + cosx | + c$

$∴ ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{2}\left(x{sec}^{2}x + tanx\right)}{( xtanx + 1{)}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{- {x}^{2}}{xtanx + 1} + 2log | xsinx + cosx | + c$

But $I ( 0 ) = 0$

$⇒ c = 0$

Also,$I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{\pi}{4} \times 1 + 1} + 2log\left|\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$= {\log}_{e}\dfrac{( \pi + 4{)}^{2}}{32} - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4 ( \pi + 4 )}$

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: If $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right|$+$ constant, then $\beta - \alpha$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right| + C$

Now solving $L . H . S$ we get,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - cos2x}{cos2x}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sqrt{2\cos^{2}x - 1}}dx$

Now let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{2{t}^{2} - 1}}$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - ln | \sqrt{2}cosx + \sqrt{cos2x} | + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|2\cos^{2}x + cos2x + 2\sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{2}cosx\right| + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|cos2x + \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{1 + cos2x}\right| + C$

Now on comparing with $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right| + C$

We get, $\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}, \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \beta - \alpha = 1$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{2x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} + 3\right)}dx$. If $f\left(3\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\log}_{e}5 - {\log}_{e}6\right)$, then $f\left(4\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$I = ∫ \dfrac{2x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} + 3\right)}dx$

Put ${x}^{2} = t ⇒ 2xdx = dt$

$I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)\left(t + 3\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{2}{\left(t + 1\right)\left(t + 3\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{t + 1} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln\left(t + 1\right) - ln\left(t + 3\right)\right] + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - ln\left({x}^{2} + 3\right)\right] + C$

Put $x = 3$, then

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln5 - ln6\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln10 - ln12\right] + C$

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln5 - ln6\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln2 + ln5 - ln2 - ln6\right] + C$

$⇒ C = 0$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[ln\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) - ln\left({x}^{2} + 3\right)\right]$

$⇒ f\left(4\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(ln17 - ln19\right)$ or $f\left(4\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\log}_{e}17 - {\log}_{e}19\right)$

questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x - 2022}{\sin^{2022}x}dx$

On rearranging we get,

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \mathop{\mathop{{sec}^{2}x}_{⏟}}_{II} \cdot \mathop{\mathop{\sin^{- 2022}x}_{⏟}}_{I}dx - 2022 ∫ \sin^{- 2022}xdx$

Now using integration by parts we get,

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = tanx . {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022} + ∫ \left(2022\right)tanx \cdot {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2023}cosxdx - 2022 ∫ {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022}dx$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = tanx . {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022} + ∫ \left(2022\right)tanx \cdot {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022}\dfrac{cosx}{sinx}dx - 2022 ∫ {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022}dx$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = tanx . {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022} + ∫ \left(2022\right){\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022}dx - 2022 ∫ {\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022}dx$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = \left(tanx\right){\left(sinx\right)}^{- 2022} + C$

Now at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = {2}^{1011} ⇒ {2}^{1011} = 1 \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{- 2022} + C ⇒ C = 0$

Hence $I\left(x\right) = \dfrac{tanx}{{\left(sinx\right)}^{2022}}$

Now finding the value of $I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2022}} = \dfrac{{2}^{2022}}{\sqrt{3}}$

And $I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2022}} = \dfrac{{2}^{2022}}{{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{2021}} = \dfrac{1}{{3}^{1010}}I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

So, ${3}^{1010}I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}sin2x\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}sin2x\right)}dx$

Multiplying by $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ in numerator and denominator, we get

$I = ∫ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + sin2x\right)}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} + sin2x}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}cosx - \dfrac{1}{2}cosx - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}sinx + \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)}{2sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)}{2sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(∫ \dfrac{dx}{sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)} - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(∫ cosec\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)dx - ∫ sec\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)dx\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(ln\left|tan\dfrac{x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}}{2}\right|\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(ln\left|tan\dfrac{x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right|\right) + C$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|\dfrac{tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}{tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}\right| + C$

questions.q: $∫ \dfrac{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right){e}^{x}}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}}dx = f\left(x\right){e}^{x} + C$, where $C$ is a constant, then $\dfrac{{d}^{3}f}{d{x}^{3}}$ at $x = 1$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right){e}^{x}dx}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}} = f\left(x\right){e}^{x} + C$

$∫ {e}^{x}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} - 1}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{2}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}}\right)dx = f\left(x\right){e}^{x} + C$

$∫ {e}^{x}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} + \dfrac{2}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}}\right)dx = f\left(x\right){e}^{x} + C$

We know that $∫ {e}^{x}\left(f\left(x\right) + {f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right) = {e}^{x}f\left(x\right) + c$

Here $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} \text{ and } {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}}$

So $∫ {e}^{x}\left(\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + \dfrac{2}{( x + 1{)}^{2}}\right)dx = f\left(x\right){e}^{x} + C$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + C = {e}^{x}f\left(x\right) + C$

On comparing both sides we get $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}$

So ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}} \text{ and } {f}^{"}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{3}}$

${f}^{'''}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{12}{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{4}}$ ,

Now ${f}^{'''}\left(1\right) = \dfrac{12}{{\left(1 + 1\right)}^{4}} = \dfrac{12}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}}dx = g\left(x\right) + c, g\left(1\right) = 0$, then $g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}}dx = g\left(x\right) + c$

Put $x = cos2\theta$

$dx = - 2sin2\theta \cdot d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{1}{cos2\theta}tan\theta\left(- 4sin\theta \cdot cos\theta\right)d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{1}{cos2\theta}\left(- 4\sin^{2}\theta\right)d\theta$

$= - 2 ∫ \dfrac{1 - cos2\theta}{cos2\theta}d\theta$

$= - \dfrac{2}{2}ln\left|sec2\theta - tan2\theta\right| + 2\theta + c$

$= ln\left|sec2\theta - tan2\theta\right| + 2\theta + c$

$= ln\left|\dfrac{1 - sin2\theta}{cos2\theta}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x + c$

$\mathop{\mathop{= ln\left|\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}{x}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x + c}_{⏟}}_{g\left(x\right)}$

$∴ g\left(1\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

So, $g\left(x\right) = ln\left|\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}{x}\right| + \cos^{- 1}x$

$g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = ln\left|2 - \sqrt{3}\right| + \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = ln\left|\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}\right| + \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e} | 1 + tanx | + \beta{\log}_{e}\left|1 - tanx + \tan^{2}x\right| + \gamma\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2tanx - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C, . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}dx$
$I = ∫ \dfrac{tanx{sec}^{2}x}{\tan^{3} + 1}dx$

Put $tanx = t ⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

$= ∫ \dfrac{tdt}{{t}^{3} + 1} = ∫ \dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)}dt$
Now $\dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} = \dfrac{A}{t + 1} + \dfrac{Bt + C}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}$

$t = A\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + ( Bt + C ) ( t + 1 )$

$t = {t}^{2}\left(A + B\right) - t\left(A - B - C\right) + A + C$

Comparing on both sides

$A + B = 0, - A + B + C = 1, A + C = 0$

Solving these equations
$A = - \dfrac{1}{3}, B = \dfrac{1}{3}, C = \dfrac{1}{3}$
Hence $I = ∫ \left\{\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{3}}{t + 1} + \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{t + 1}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}\right)\right\}dt$
$= - \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)}dt + \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}\left(2t - 1\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}dt$

$= - \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)}dt + \dfrac{1}{6} ∫ \dfrac{2t - 1}{\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2}}$= - \dfrac{1}{3}ln\left|t + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{6}ln\left|{t}^{2} - t + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2t - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{3}ln\left|tanx + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{6}ln\left|\tan^{2}x - tanx + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2tanx - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C$

From equation $\left(i\right)$, Comparing from both sides
$⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{3}, \beta = \dfrac{1}{6}$ and $\gamma = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
So $18\left(\alpha + \beta + {\gamma}^{2}\right)$

$= 18\left(- \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$= 3$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}dx\left(x \ge 0\right)$. Then $f\left(3\right) - f\left(1\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}dx$

Let $x = \tan^{2}\theta$

$dx = 2tan\theta{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{tan\theta}{{\left(1 + \tan^{2}\theta\right)}^{2}} . 2tan\theta{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{tan\theta}{{sec}^{4}\theta} . 2tan\theta{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ 2\tan^{2}\theta . \cos^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ 2\sin^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left(1 - cos2\theta\right)d\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = \theta - \dfrac{sin2\theta}{2} + C = \theta - \dfrac{tan\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta} + C$

$f\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x} + C$

Now, $f\left(3\right) - f\left(1\right) = \tan^{-}\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1 + 3} - \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{1} + \dfrac{1}{1 + 1}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{12} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$

questions.q: If $∫ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x}\right)dx = A\left(x\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) + B\left(x\right) + C$, where $C$ is a constant of integration, then the ordered pair $\left(A\left(x\right), B\left(x\right)\right)$ can be :
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x}\right)dx$

$= ∫ \mathop{\mathop{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{I}\mathop{\mathop{\left(1\right)}_{⏟}}_{II}dx$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + x} . \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} . xdx + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{t . 2t . dt}{1 + {t}^{2}} + C ($putting $x = {t}^{2} ⇒ dx = 2tdt )$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{1 + {t}^{2}}dt + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - t + \tan^{- 1}t + C$

$= x\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} + C$

$= \left(x + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + C$

Comparing with $A\left(x\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) + B\left(x\right) + C$, we get

$\left(A\left(x\right), B\left(x\right)\right) = \left(x + 1, - \sqrt{x}\right)$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{d\theta}{\cos^{2}\theta\left(tan2\theta + sec2\theta\right)} = \lambdatan\theta + 2{\log}_{e}\left|f\left(\theta\right)\right| + C$ where $C$ is a constant of integration, then the ordered pair $\left(\lambda, f\left(\theta\right)\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}\theta}{\dfrac{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}{1 - \tan^{2}\theta} + \dfrac{2tan\theta}{1 - \tan^{2}\theta}}d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}\theta\left(1 - \tan^{2}\theta\right)}{{\left(1 + tan\theta\right)}^{2}}d\theta$

$= ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}\theta\left(1 - tan\theta\right)}{1 + tan\theta}d\theta$

Let $tan\theta = t ⇒ {sec}^{2}\thetad\theta = dt$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t}\right)dt = ∫ \left(- 1 + \dfrac{2}{1 + t}\right)dt$

$= - t + 2ln\left(1 + t\right) + C$

$= - tan\theta + 2ln\left(1 + tan\theta\right) + C$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1andf\left(\theta\right) = 1 + tan\theta$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1andf\left(\theta\right) = 1 + tan\theta$

questions.q: Let $\alpha \in ( 0, \dfrac{\pi}{2} )$, be constant.If the integral $∫ \dfrac{tanx + tan\alpha}{tanx - tan\alpha}dx = A\left(x\right)cos2\alpha + B\left(x\right)sin2\alpha + C$, where C is a constant of integration, then the functions $A ( x )$ and $B ( x )$ are respectively
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{tanx + tan\alpha}{tanx - tan\alpha}dx = ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{sinx}{cosx} + \dfrac{sin\alpha}{cos\alpha}}{\dfrac{sinx}{cosx} - \dfrac{sin\alpha}{cos\alpha}}dx$
$= ∫ \dfrac{sinxcos\alpha + cosxsin\alpha}{sinxcos\alpha - cosxsin\alpha}dx = ∫ \dfrac{sin\left(x + \alpha\right)}{sin\left(x - \alpha\right)}dx$
$= ∫ \dfrac{sin\left(\left(x - \alpha\right) + 2\alpha\right)}{sin ( x - \alpha )}dx = ∫ \dfrac{sin\left(x - \alpha\right)cos2\alpha + cos\left(x - \alpha\right)sin2\alpha}{sin ( x - \alpha )}dx$
$= ∫ \left[cos2\alpha + sin2\alphacot\left(x - \alpha\right)\right]dx$
$= xcos2\alpha + sin2\alpha{\log}_{e}\left|sin\left(x - \alpha\right)\right| + C$
$= ( x - \alpha ) cos2\alpha + sin2\alpha{\log}_{e}\left|sin\left(x - \alpha\right)\right| + C$
Hence, $A\left(x\right) = x - \alpha$ and $B\left(x\right) = lo{g}_{e}\left|sin\left(x - \alpha\right)\right|$

questions.q: If $∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx = g\left(x\right){e}^{- {x}^{2}} + c$, where $c$ is a constant of integration, then $g\left(- 1\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = ∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx$

Let, $- {x}^{2} = t ⇒ xdx = - \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$∴ I = - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ {t}^{2}{e}^{t}dt$

By using integrating by parts, i.e. $∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}u ∫ vdx\right]dx + c,$ we get

$I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2} ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ \left(2t ∫ {e}^{t}dt\right)dt\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2 ∫ t{e}^{t}dt\right] + c$

Again, applying integrating by parts, we get

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ 1 \cdot {e}^{t}dt\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t{e}^{t} - {e}^{t}\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2t{e}^{t} + 2{e}^{t}\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{e}^{t}}{2}\left[{t}^{2} - 2t + 2\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{e}^{- {x}^{2}}}{2}\left[{x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 2\right] + c$

Given, $I = ∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx = g\left(x\right){e}^{- {x}^{2}} + c$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left({x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ g\left(- 1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\left(- 1\right)}^{4} + 2{\left(- 1\right)}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ g\left(- 1\right) = - \dfrac{5}{2} .$
questions.question: If $∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx = g\left(x\right){e}^{- {x}^{2}} + c$, where $c$ is a constant of integration, then $g\left(- 1\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Let $I = ∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx$

Let, $- {x}^{2} = t ⇒ xdx = - \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$∴ I = - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ {t}^{2}{e}^{t}dt$

By using integrating by parts, i.e. $∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}u ∫ vdx\right]dx + c,$ we get

$I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2} ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ \left(2t ∫ {e}^{t}dt\right)dt\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2 ∫ t{e}^{t}dt\right] + c$

Again, applying integrating by parts, we get

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ 1 \cdot {e}^{t}dt\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t{e}^{t} - {e}^{t}\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2t{e}^{t} + 2{e}^{t}\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{e}^{t}}{2}\left[{t}^{2} - 2t + 2\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{e}^{- {x}^{2}}}{2}\left[{x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 2\right] + c$

Given, $I = ∫ {x}^{5}{e}^{- {x}^{2}}dx = g\left(x\right){e}^{- {x}^{2}} + c$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left({x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ g\left(- 1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\left(- 1\right)}^{4} + 2{\left(- 1\right)}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ g\left(- 1\right) = - \dfrac{5}{2} .$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left({x}^{2} - 2x + 10\right)}^{2}} = A\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right) + \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{{x}^{2} - 2x + 10}\right) + C$, then (where $C$ is a constant of integration)
questions.solution:
We have $I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left({x}^{2} - 2x + 10\right)}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left[{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {3}^{2}\right]}^{2}}$

Let $x – 1 = 3tan\theta ⇒ dx = 3{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{3se{c}^{2}\thetad\theta}{81se{c}^{4}\theta} = \dfrac{1}{27} ∫ co{s}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$= \dfrac{1}{54} ∫ \left(1 + cos2\theta\right)d\theta$

$= \dfrac{1}{54}\left(\theta + \dfrac{sin2\theta}{2}\right) + C$

$= \dfrac{1}{54}\left(\theta + sin\thetacos\theta\right) + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration.

$= \dfrac{1}{54}\left[\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right) + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right)}{1 + {\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right)}^{2}}\right] + C$

$= \dfrac{1}{54}\left[ta{n}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right) + \dfrac{3\left(x - 1\right)}{{x}^{2} - 2x + 10}\right] + C$

Hence, $A = \dfrac{1}{54} \text{ and } f\left(x\right) = 3 ( x - 1 )$

questions.q: If $∫ {e}^{secx}\left(secxtanxf\left(x\right) + \left(secxtanx + se{c}^{2}x\right)\right)dx = {e}^{secx}f\left(x\right) + C,$ then a possible choice of $f\left(x\right)$ is:

$∫ {e}^{sec ⁡ x} ( sec ⁡ xtan ⁡ xf\left(x\right) + \left(sec ⁡ xtan ⁡ x + {sec}^{2} ⁡ x\right)dx = {e}^{sec ⁡ x}f\left(x\right) + C$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t $‘x’$ we get

${e}^{secx}\left(secxtanxf\left(x\right) + \left(secxtanx + {sec}^{2}x\right)\right) = \left({e}^{secx} ⋅ secxtanx\right)f ( x ) + {e}^{secx}{f}^{'}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {sec}^{2}x + tanxsecx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left({sec}^{2}x + tanxsecx\right)dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = tanx + secx + c, c \in R$
Hence, possible choice is $f\left(x\right) = secx + tanx + \dfrac{1}{2} .$

questions.q: $∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{5x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$, is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{5x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{sin\left(2x + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

Using $sin\left(A + B\right) = sinAcosB + cosAsinB$

$= ∫ \dfrac{sin2xcos\dfrac{x}{2} + cos2xsin\dfrac{x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{\left(2sinxcosx\right)cos\dfrac{x}{2}}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}} + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{2\left(2sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right)cosxcos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{x}{2}} + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)cosx + cos2x\right)dx$

Using $cos2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1 ⇒ 2\cos^{2}x = 1 + cos2x$

$= ∫ \left(2\left(1 + cosx\right)cosx + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + 2\cos^{2}x + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + \left(1 + cos2x\right) + cos2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(2cosx + 2cos2x + 1\right)dx$

$= 2sinx + sin2x + x + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration.

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{3{x}^{13} + 2{x}^{11}}{{\left(2{x}^{4} + 3{x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{4}}dx$, is equal to
questions.solution:
The given integral can be written as

$I = ∫ \dfrac{3 . {x}^{- 3} + 2{x}^{- 5}}{{\left(2 + 3{x}^{- 2} + {x}^{- 4}\right)}^{4}}dx$

(Dividing ${x}^{16}$ to both numerator and denominator),

Let, $2 + 3{x}^{- 2} + {x}^{- 4} = t$

$⇒ \left(- 6{x}^{- 3} - 4{x}^{- 5}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ - 2\left(3{x}^{- 3} + 2{x}^{- 5}\right)dx = dt$

$∴ I = - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{4}} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{{t}^{- 4 + 1}}{- 4 + 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{1}{{t}^{3}}\right) + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration.

$= \dfrac{1}{6{\left(2 + 3{x}^{- 2} + {x}^{- 4}\right)}^{3}} + C = \dfrac{{x}^{12}}{6{\left(2{x}^{4} + 3{x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{3}} + C$

Let, $2 + 3{x}^{- 2} + {x}^{- 4} = t$

$⇒ \left(- 6{x}^{- 3} - 4{x}^{- 5}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ - 2\left(3{x}^{- 3} + 2{x}^{- 5}\right)dx = dt$

questions.q:
If $\int \frac{x+1}{\sqrt{2 x-1}} \mathrm{~d} x=f(x) \sqrt{2 x-1}+\mathrm{C},$ where $\mathrm{C}$ is a constant

of integration, then $f(x)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \frac{x+1}{\sqrt{2 x-1}} d x$

Put $\sqrt{2 x-1}=t$\begin{array}{l}

\therefore \quad 2 x-1=t^{2} \Rightarrow d x=t d t \\

I=\int \frac{\left(t^{2}+3\right)}{2} d t=\frac{t^{3}}{6}+\frac{3 t}{2}+C \\

=\frac{(2 x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{6}+\frac{3}{2}(2 x-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}+C \\

=\sqrt{2 x-1}\left(\frac{x+4}{3}\right)+C \\

=f(x) \cdot \sqrt{2 x-1}+C

\end{array}$

Hence, $f(x)=\frac{x+4}{3}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x^{4}} d x=A(\mathrm{x})\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{m}+C,$ for a suitable chosen integer $\mathrm{m}$ and a function $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{x})$, where $\mathrm{C}$ is a constant of integration, then $(\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{x}))^{\mathrm{m}}$ equals :
questions.solution:
$A(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{m}+C=\int \frac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x^{4}} d x$=\int \frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1}}{x^{3}} d x$

Let $\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1=u^{2}$\Rightarrow-\frac{2}{x^{3}}=\frac{2 u d u}{d x}$\frac{d x}{x^{3}}=-u d u$A(x)\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{m}+C=\int\left(-u^{2}\right) d u=-\frac{u^{3}}{3}+C$\begin{array}{l}

=-\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}-1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C \\

=-\frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{x^{3}} \cdot\left(1-x^{2}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C \\

=\frac{-1}{3 x^{3}}\left(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)^{3}+C

\end{array}$

Compare both sides,

$\begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow A(x)=-\frac{1}{3 x^{3}} \text{ and } m=3 \\

\Rightarrow(A(x))^{3}=\frac{-1}{27 x^{9}}

\end{array}$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = - 4{x}^{3} - 1$

questions.q: Let, $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$ Then $∫ \dfrac{\left(si{n}^{n}\theta - sin\theta\right)\dfrac{1}{n}cos\theta}{si{n}^{n + 1}\theta}d\theta,$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{\left(\sin^{n}\theta - sin\theta\right)\dfrac{1}{n}cos\theta}{\sin^{n + 1}\theta}d\theta$

Put, $sin\theta = t ⇒ cos\thetad\theta = dt$

$= \begin{cases}∫ \dfrac{\left({t}^{n} - t\right)\dfrac{1}{n}dt}{{t}^{n + 1}} & \end{cases}$

$= ∫ \dfrac{t\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{n - 1}}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}{{t}^{n + 1}}dt$

$= ∫ \dfrac{{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{n - 1}}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}{{t}^{n}}dt$

Put $1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{n - 1}} = z$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)}{{t}^{n}}dt = dz$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{n - 1} ∫ z\dfrac{1}{n}dz$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1} + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{z}^{\dfrac{1}{n} + 1}}{\left(\dfrac{1}{n} + 1\right)\left(n - 1\right)} + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{n{\left(1 - {t}^{1 - n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n} + 1}}{{n}^{2} - 1} + c,$ where $c$ is the constant of integration.
$⇒ I = \dfrac{n}{{n}^{2} - 1}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sin^{n - 1}\theta}\right)\dfrac{n + 1}{n} + c .$

$= ∫ \dfrac{t\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{n - 1}}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}{{t}^{n + 1}}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{n}{{n}^{2} - 1}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sin^{n - 1}\theta}\right)\dfrac{n + 1}{n} + c .$

Now, $f(x)=2\left(\frac{2 x+4}{1-x}\right)+1=\frac{3 x+9}{1-x} \begin{aligned}$&=$\frac{3(x+3)}{1-x}=\frac{3(x-1+4)}{1-x}=-3+\frac{12}{1-x}\\
&\therefore \int$ f(x) d x=-12 $\log _e|1-x|-3 x+c$
\end{aligned}

questions.q: If $f\left(\dfrac{x - 4}{x + 2}\right) = 2x + 1, \left(x \in R - \left\{1, - 2\right\}\right)$, then$∫ f\left(x\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $f\left(\dfrac{x - 4}{x + 2}\right) = 2x + 1$

Let $\dfrac{x - 4}{x + 2} = X ⇒ xX + 2X = x - 4 ⇒ x\left(X - 1\right) = - 4 - 2X ⇒ x = \dfrac{2\left(2 + X\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$

Putting $x = \dfrac{2\left(2 + X\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$ in the given functional equation, we get

$⇒ f\left(X\right) = 2 \times 2\left\{\dfrac{2 + X}{1 - X}\right\} + 1 = \dfrac{8 + 4X + 1 - X}{1 - X} = \dfrac{3X + 9}{1 - X} = \dfrac{3\left(X + 3\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$

Replacing $X \to x$, we get

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{3\left(x + 3\right)}{\left(1 - x\right)}$

$⇒ ∫ f\left(x\right)dx = 3 ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 3}{1 - x}\right)dx = 3 ∫ \dfrac{4 - \left(1 - x\right)}{1 - x}dx = 3\left\{∫ \dfrac{4}{1 - x}dx - ∫ dx\right\}$

$= - 12ln\left|1 - x\right| - 3x + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration.

We have, $f\left(\dfrac{x - 4}{x + 2}\right) = 2x + 1$

Let $\dfrac{x - 4}{x + 2} = X ⇒ xX + 2X = x - 4 ⇒ x\left(X - 1\right) = - 4 - 2X ⇒ x = \dfrac{2\left(2 + X\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$

Putting $x = \dfrac{2\left(2 + X\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$ in the given functional equation, we get

$⇒ f\left(X\right) = 2 \times 2\left\{\dfrac{2 + X}{1 - X}\right\} + 1 = \dfrac{8 + 4X + 1 - X}{1 - X} = \dfrac{3X + 9}{1 - X} = \dfrac{3\left(X + 3\right)}{\left(1 - X\right)}$

Replacing $X \to x$, we get

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{3\left(x + 3\right)}{\left(1 - x\right)}$

$⇒ ∫ f\left(x\right)dx = 3 ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 3}{1 - x}\right)dx = 3 ∫ \dfrac{4 - \left(1 - x\right)}{1 - x}dx = 3\left\{∫ \dfrac{4}{1 - x}dx - ∫ dx\right\}$

$= - 12ln\left|1 - x\right| - 3x + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration.

questions.solution:
Given $f\left(\dfrac{3x - 4}{3x + 4}\right) = x + 2, x \ne - \dfrac{4}{3}$

Let, $\dfrac{3x - 4}{3x + 4} = t$

$3x - 4 = 3tx + 4t$

$x = \dfrac{4t + 4}{3 - 3t} + 2$

$∴ f\left(t\right) = \dfrac{10 - 2t}{3 - 3t}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2x - 10}{3x - 3}$

$∫ f\left(x\right)dx = ∫ \dfrac{2x - 10}{3x - 3}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{2x}{3x - 3}dx - 10 ∫ \dfrac{dx}{3x - 3}$

$= \dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}ln\left|x - 1\right| + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration.

questions.solution:
Let $I = ∫ \sqrt{1 + 2cotx\left(cosecx + cotx\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left(\sqrt{2cotxcosecx + {cosec}^{2}x + {cot}^{2}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \sqrt{{\left(cosecx + cotx\right)}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left|cosecx + cotx\right|dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left(cosecx + cotx\right)dx$

$⇒ I = log\left|tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right| + log\left|sinx\right| + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration.
$⇒ I = log\left(\dfrac{sin\dfrac{x}{2}}{cos\dfrac{x}{2}} \cdot 2sin\dfrac{x}{2}cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + c$
$⇒ I = 2log\left|sin\dfrac{x}{2}\right| + c$

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + \sqrt{x}\right)\sqrt{x - {x}^{2}}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + \sqrt{x}\right)\sqrt{x}\sqrt{1 - x}}$

Put, $1 + \sqrt{x} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}dx = dt$

And, $1 - x = 1 - {\left(t - 1\right)}^{2} = 2t - {t}^{2}$

$∴ I = ∫ \dfrac{2dt}{t\sqrt{2t - {t}^{2}}}$

Again put, $t = \dfrac{1}{z} ⇒ dt = \dfrac{- 1}{{z}^{2}}dz$

$⇒ I = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}dz}{\dfrac{1}{z}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{z} - \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}}} = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- dz}{\sqrt{2z - 1}} = - 2\sqrt{2z - 1} + c$

Where $c$ is arbitrary constant.

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{t} - 1} + c$

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{2 - t}{t}} + c$

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{x}}{1 + \sqrt{x}}} + c$
questions.question: The integral $∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + \sqrt{x}\right)\sqrt{x - {x}^{2}}}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + \sqrt{x}\right)\sqrt{x}\sqrt{1 - x}}$

Put, $1 + \sqrt{x} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}dx = dt$

And, $1 - x = 1 - {\left(t - 1\right)}^{2} = 2t - {t}^{2}$

$∴ I = ∫ \dfrac{2dt}{t\sqrt{2t - {t}^{2}}}$

Again put, $t = \dfrac{1}{z} ⇒ dt = \dfrac{- 1}{{z}^{2}}dz$

$⇒ I = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}dz}{\dfrac{1}{z}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{z} - \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}}} = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- dz}{\sqrt{2z - 1}} = - 2\sqrt{2z - 1} + c$

Where $c$ is arbitrary constant.

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{t} - 1} + c$

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{2 - t}{t}} + c$

$= - 2\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{x}}{1 + \sqrt{x}}} + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}dt = dz$

$∴ g\left(t\right) = log\left(t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(2\right) = log\left(2 + \sqrt{1 + 4}\right)$

Hence, $log\left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right)$, is the answer.

$∴ ∫ \dfrac{- dt}{m{t}^{3}} = f\left(x\right) + c$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1} + C, n \ne - 1$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{m}\left(\dfrac{{t}^{- 2}}{- 2}\right) = f\left(x\right) + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2m{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{m}} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2m}}\right)}^{2}} + c = f\left(x\right) + c$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2m}\dfrac{{x}^{4m}}{{\left({x}^{2m} + {x}^{m} + 1\right)}^{2}} = f\left(x\right) .$

questions.q: $\text{ The integral } \int \frac{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}{\left(\sin ^3 x+\cos ^3 x\right)^2}$d x $\text{ is equal to: }$
options:
$\frac{1}{\left(1+\cot ^3 x\right.}+c$

$\left.-\frac{1}{3\left(1+\tan ^3 x\right.}+c\right)$

$\frac{\sin ^3 x}{\left(1+\cos ^3 x\right.}+c$

$-\frac{\cos ^3 x}{3\left(1+\sin ^3 x\right.}+c$
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \frac{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}{\left(\sin ^3 x+\cos ^3 x\right)^2} d x\begin{aligned}$&$\mathrm{I}=\int\left(\frac{\sin x \cdot \cos x}{\sin ^3 x+\cos ^3 x}\right)^$2 d x \\
&$\mathrm{I}=\int\left(\frac{\sin x \cdot \cos x}{\cos ^3 x\left(1+\tan ^3 x\right)}\right)^$2 d x \\
&=$\int\left(\frac{\sin x \cdot \sec ^2 x}{\left(1+\tan ^3 x\right)}\right)^$2 d x \\
&$\text{ Put }$1+\tan ^3 x=$\mathrm{t}$\\
&d t=3 \tan ^2 x \sec ^2 x d x $\text{$ or }d x \\
&=$\frac{d t}{3 \tan ^2 x \sec ^2 x}$\\
&\therefore $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\sin ^2 x \cdot \sec ^4 x}{t^2} \times \frac{d t}{3 \tan ^2 x \sec ^2 x}
\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}$&$\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{\sin ^2 x \cdot \sec ^4 x}{t^2} \times \frac{d t}{\frac{\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x} \times \sec ^2 x}$\\
&=$\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{\sin ^2 x \cdot \sec ^4 x}{t^2} \times \frac{d t}{\sin ^2 x \sec ^4 x}$\\
&\therefore $\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{d t}{t^2}=\frac{1}{3} \int$t^{-2} d t \\
&$\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}\left[\frac{t^{-2+1}}{-2+1}\right]+$c=$\frac{-1}{3}\left[\frac{1}{t}\right]+$c \\
&$\text{$ or $} \mathrm{I}=-\frac{1}{3\left(1+\tan ^3 x\right)}+$c
\end{aligned}

questions.q: The integral $\int x \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right) d x(x>0)$ is equal to:

$\mathrm{I}=2\left[\frac{x^2}{2} \tan ^{-1}$ x-$\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} \times \frac{x^2}{2}$ d x\right]+c \\
$\mathrm{I}=2\left[\frac{x^2}{2} \tan ^{-1}$ x-$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{x^2+1-1}{x^2+1}$ d x\right]+c \\
$\mathrm{I}=2\left[\frac{x^2}{2} \tan ^{-1}$ x-$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{x^2+1}{x^2+1}$ d x+$\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{1+x^2}$ d x\right]+c
\end{array}

$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{I}$&=2$\left[\frac{x^2}{2} \tan ^{-1}$ x-$\frac{1}{2} \int1 . d x+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}$ x\right]+c \\

$\mathrm{I}$&=x² \tan ^{-1} x+\tan ^{-1} x-x+c \\
& $\text{ or }$ I=-x+$\left($ x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+c

questions.q:
If the integral

$\int \frac{\cos 8 x+1}{\cot 2 x-\tan 2 x}$d x=A \cos 8 x+k

where $k$ is an arbitrary constant, then $\mathrm{A}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\cos 8 x+1}{\cot 2 x-\tan 2 x} d x$
Now, $\mathrm{D}^r=\cot 2 x-\tan 2 x=\frac{\cos 2 x}{\sin 2 x}-\frac{\sin 2 x}{\cos 2 x}$
=$\frac{\cos ^2 2 x-\sin ^2 2 x}{\sin 2 x \cos 2 x}=\frac{2 \cos 4 x}{\sin 4 x}\begin{aligned} \therefore \mathrm{I} &=\int \frac{2 \cos ^2 4 x}{\frac{2 \cos 4 x}{\sin 4 x}} d x=\int \frac{2 \cos ^2 4 x \cdot \sin 4 x}{2 \cos 4 x} d x \\ &=\frac{1}{2} \int \sin 8 x d x=-\frac{1}{2} \frac{\cos 8 x}{8}+k \\ &=-\frac{1}{16} \cdot \cos 8 x+k \\ & \text{ Now },-\frac{1}{16} \cdot \cos 8 x+k=\mathrm{A} \cos 8 x+k \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=-\frac{1}{16} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+1} e^{\cot ^{-1} x} d x=A(x) e^{\cot ^{-1} x}+C$, then $A(x)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+1} \cdot e^{\cot ^{-1} x} d x$
Put $x=\cot t \Rightarrow-\operatorname{cosec}^2 t d t=d x$
Now, $1+\cot ^2 t=\operatorname{cosec}^2 t\therefore\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{e^t\left(\cot ^2 t-\cot t+1\right)}{\left(1+\cot ^2 t\right)}\left(-\operatorname{cosec}^2 t\right) d t \begin{aligned}$& =-$\int$e^t$\left(\operatorname{cosec}{ }^$2 t-\cot t\right) d t \\
& =$\int$e^t$\left(\cot$t-\operatorname{cosec}^2 t\right) d t \\
& =e^t \cot t+$\mathrm{C}$\\
& =e^{\cot ^{-1} x}(x)+$\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{A}($x) $\cdot$e^{\cot ^{-1} x}+$\mathrm{C}$\\
\Rightarrow $\mathrm{A}($x) & =x
\end{aligned}

questions.q: If $f(x)=\int\left(\frac{x^2+\sin ^2 x}{1+x^2}\right) \sec ^2 x d x$ and $f(0)=0$, then $f(1)$ equals
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Let }$f(x)=$\int\left(\frac{x^2+\sin ^2 x}{1+x^2}\right) \sec ^$2 x d x \\
& =$\int \frac{x^2 \sec ^2 x+\frac{\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x}}{1+x^2}$d x
\end{aligned}

$\begin{aligned}$& =$\int \frac{x^2 \sec ^2 x+\tan ^2 x}{1+x^2}$d x \\
& =$\int \frac{x^2\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)+\tan ^2 x}{1+x^2}$d x \\
& =$\int \frac{x^2+\tan ^2 x\left(1+x^2\right)}{1+x^2}$d x \\
& =$\int \frac{x^2}{1+x^2}$d x+$\int \tan ^$2 x d x \\
& =$\int \frac{x^2+1-1}{1+x^2} \mathrm{dx}+\int\left(\sec ^$2 $\mathrm{x}-$1 $\mathrm{dx}\right.$\\
& =$\int$1 d x-$\int \frac{d x}{1+x^2}+\int \sec ^$2 x d x-$\int$d x \\
& =-\tan -1 x+\tan ^{-1} x+$\mathrm{c}$\\
& $\text{ Given: }$f(0)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow f(0)=-\tan ^{-1} 0+\tan ^2+c \\
& \Rightarrow c=0 \\
& \therefore f(x)=-\tan ^{-1} x+\tan ^2 x
\end{aligned}

Now,

f(1)=-\tan ^{-1}(1)+\tan 1=\tan 1-$\frac{\pi}{4}$

$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Let } f(x)=\int\left(\frac{x^2+\sin ^2 x}{1+x^2}\right) \sec ^2 x d x \\
& =\int \frac{x^2 \sec ^2 x+\frac{\sin ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x}}{1+x^2} d x
\end{aligned}
 
\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{x^2 \sec ^2 x+\tan ^2 x}{1+x^2} d x \\
& =\int \frac{x^2\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)+\tan ^2 x}{1+x^2} d x \\
& =\int \frac{x^2+\tan ^2 x\left(1+x^2\right)}{1+x^2} d x \\

$

$

questions.q: The value of $\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x d x}{\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}$ is
questions.solution:
$
\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x d x}{\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}=\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) d x}{\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} \\
& =\sqrt{2} \int\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}+\cot \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sin \frac{\pi}{4}\right) d x \\
& =\int d x+\int \cot \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) d x \\
& =x+\ln \left|\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right|+c .
\end{aligned}
$

& =\frac{e^t}{1+t^2}+c=\frac{x}{1+(\log x)^2}+c
\end{aligned}
$
